title: Event propagation phases
learningObjectives: Explain event propagation phases and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: DOM events propagate through capture, target, and bubble phases. Capture travels from ancestors toward the target; the event reaches the target; bubbling travels back through ancestors when the event bubbles. Event listeners can select a phase using the capture option.
understand.whyItMatters: Propagation explains why a parent listener can respond to a child interaction and how delegated event handling works. Knowing the phase helps avoid accidental duplicate handling.
understand.analogy: An event travels down a chain to its destination and may travel back up the chain afterward.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: Clicking the child logs the capture listener first, then the target listener, then the bubbling listener.

examples.explanation: Clicking the child logs the capture listener first, then the target listener, then the bubbling listener.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Add listeners on an outer section, inner div, and button for capture and bubble. Record the order.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: What are the three common event propagation phases?
questions.explanation: DOM event propagation consists of capture, target, and bubbling phases.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
